cues: Hello sisters, this is Naheed.
Before we begin, please do not listen to this while driving
or while doing anything that needs your full attention.
Find a safe place to sit or lie down.
This is a short relaxation practice.
It is not a medical advice, and it is not a treatment.
If sleep problems continue, please speak to your doctor.
Alright, let's take these five minutes just for you.
Get comfortable.
Let your shoulders drop.
Let your shoulders drop away from your ears.
Let your hands rest wherever they are comfortable.
If your eyes are open, let them soften.
If it feels comfortable,
you can close them.
Now notice the sounds around you.
A fan,
a distant car,
the quiet of the room.
You don't need to do anything with them.
Just let them be there.
There is nothing you need to fix right now.
Nothing you need to finish.
This is your time.
Let's breathe slowly, gently,
no forcing, belly breathing.
When you are breathing, the belly goes out.
When you are exhaling, the belly goes in.
Breathe in through your nose for a count of four.
One, two, three, four.
And breathe out slowly through your mouth with a sigh for a count of six.
One, two, three, four, five, six.
Again in through the nose.
Two, three, four.
And out slowly.
Two, three, four, five, six.
One more time.
In, two, three, four.
And out, two, three, four, five, six.
Now let your breathing go back to its natural rhythm.
You don't need to control it anymore.
Bring your attention now to your forehead.
Let it be soft, smooth.
Feel relaxed.
More relaxed.
Let your jaw loosen.
Let your teeth part slightly.
Relax.
Let your neck and shoulders feel heavy.
Loosen them.
Feel relaxed.
Let your arm feel heavy all the way to your fingertips.
Notice your chest rising and falling on its own.
Let your stomach be soft.
You don't need to hold it tonight.
Relax.
Let your legs feel heavy, more heavy, more heavier.
And your feet feel warm, relaxed.
Feel relaxed.
Now think of one thing from today that you can let go.
Just one.
A worry,
a task, a conversation.
And as you breathe out, imagine setting it down.
It will still be there tomorrow if you need it.
But for tonight, you can put it down.
You have done something kind to yourself in this few minutes.
I acknowledge you.
I appreciate you.
And you can come back to this any evening.
When you are ready, take one deep breath in and out.
If you would like to continue resting,
stay as you are.
If you need to get up,
gently move your fingers and toes and open your eyes.
Thank you for taking this time.
Be kind to yourself tonight.
Good night.
